fields.detail: The correct mod-q consistency for the unbounded equation sum_{a in A}3^a = 2^n is (b'): exists digit-free high part s with 2^r = L_r + 3^k s (mod M'). cross_modulus_corrected.py proved Dr(q)=F_q for the 10 prime q in Q_LIST. cross_modulus_coverage_general.py (THIS RUN) generalised to ALL M' coprime to 3 in [2,300] (199 moduli, primes AND composites incl. 8,16,25,80,121,128,242), 0 failures, by the s_t = sum_{j<t} 3^{jm} witness (m=ord_{M'}(3); each term distinct power of 3 so digit-free, each =1 mod M' so s_t=t mod M'). Independent brute-force Dr(M')==F_{M'} confirmed for M'=8,16,25,80. CONCLUSION: the corrected condition (b') is VACUOUS for every M' coprime to 3 (proved by witness, verified-numerically M'<=300), so the RELAXED (exists-digit-free-s) mixed-modulus route cannot drive |A_k| below 2^(k-1) with any M'. This refutes the relaxed reading of H1 of CROSS-MODULUS-BEATS-SIEVE-HYPOTHESES. Capture: code/out/cross_modulus_coverage_general.captured.txt, EXIT 0.

Settled this run. order of 3 mod 2^r == 2^(r-2) verified for r=3..40. The identity sum_c N_c 3^c == 2^n (mod 2^r) with N_c=#{a in A: a==c mod 2^(r-2)} is EXACT (a tautology) on every digit-2-free n: it is just regrouping 2^n=sum_{a in A}3^a by a mod ord, using ord_{2^r}(3)=2^(r-2). Verified 0 failures on the digit-free survivors in [0,1000]={0,2,8} across r=3..12. So the 2-adic family CANNOT close by itself: it imposes no exclusion. Survivor-exponent coverage of even 2-adic classes: at k=8 every even class mod 2^m is covered for m=3..6; at small k (k=4,6) some m exceed coverage (e.g. k=4 m=6: only 8 of 32 even classes). So the prior memory that survivors 'fill every even 2-adic class' holds only ASYMPTOTICALLY in k, not at fixed small k. Capture: code/out/verify_2adic_family.captured.txt, EXIT 0.

fields.reason: Settled. code/out/verify_2adic_family.captured.txt (EXIT 0): order of 3 mod 2^r == 2^(r-2) for r=3..40 ALL OK; the congruence sum_c N_c 3^c == 2^n (mod 2^r) is a tautology on digit-free n (0 failures on {0,2,8} across r=3..12), because it only regroups 2^n=sum 3^a by a mod 2^(r-2). Hence the family imposes no exclusion and cannot close. Survivor classes cover all even 2-adic classes only asymptotically in k (k=8 covers all even mod 2^6; k=4 misses many), correcting the prior over-strong phrasing.
